body.x: ORPHE Inc., a Japan-based startup specializing in gait analysis and smart footwear technology, is showcasing its ORPHE INSOLE at CES 2026, where the product has been named a Best of Innovation Award winner in the CES Innovation Awards 2026.

ORPHE INSOLE is designed to bring lab-grade biomechanical analysis into everyday footwear. The system integrates a six-axis inertial measurement unit (IMU) and six pressure sensors per foot, enabling continuous tracking of motion and pressure during daily activities. According to the company, the insole lasts more than 24 hours on a single charge, supports real-time Bluetooth data streaming, wireless and magnetic charging, and offers an open-source software development kit compatible with Python and JavaScript.

The company positions the product as a solution to long-standing limitations in gait analysis, which has traditionally relied on expensive force plates, laboratory environments, and expert interpretation. ORPHE aims to enable real-world data collection by allowing users to generate movement logs simply by wearing smart shoes, with data aggregated in the cloud and accessible to medical professionals via an API.

At the core of the technology is ORPHE’s dual-sensing approach, which fuses motion data from the IMU with plantar pressure data sampled at up to 200 Hz. The system also incorporates edge computing, allowing real-time gait analysis and machine-learning inference directly on the device without reliance on cloud processing. A proprietary algorithm based on Zero-Velocity Updates (ZUPTs) is used to reduce sensor drift and improve the accuracy of distance, posture, and gait calculations.

ORPHE’s technology is already being used in healthcare and research settings. The company reports that its ORPHE ANALYTICS MEDICAL platform is currently deployed in dozens of medical institutions across Japan for daily gait evaluations, including post-orthopedic surgery assessments. Ongoing research projects also include rehabilitation for Parkinson’s disease, using smart shoes to detect freezing of gait and deliver real-time auditory cues, as well as industrial safety applications developed in collaboration with Mitsubishi Materials to prevent workplace falls.

In addition to medical and research use cases, ORPHE has partnered with ASICS since 2019 to develop smart running and walking shoes. Previous collaborations include EVORIDE ORPHE and RUNWALK ORPHE, which integrate ORPHE’s motion sensors into commercial footwear.

Founded in 2014 and headquartered in Shibuya, Tokyo, ORPHE Inc. focuses on the research, development, and commercialization of DX and IoT-based gait analysis solutions for healthcare, sports, and industrial applications. The company holds multiple patents and has received several design and innovation awards in Japan. Its corporate mission is summarized as “Sensing Feet, Changing Everything.”

At CES 2026, ORPHE is exhibiting at the Venetian Campus, Venetian Expo, Level 2, Halls A–D, at booth number 54199, seeking research partners and global collaborators to expand its smart footwear platform into international markets.
